To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
systemic antiviral therapy is effective in decreasing the incidence of latent herpes simplex virus in the trigemini ganglia of mice.

(a) systemic antiviral drug treatment is effective in preventing the establishment of latent herpes simplex virus in mice; (b) the effectiveness of the therapy is related to the time of treatment initiation after infection; (c) the effectiveness of treatment decreases with time after infection and (d) the effectiveness of therapy is related to both the duration and the dose of the antiviral drug used.
systemic antiviral treatment can reduce the incidence of latent HSV in the ganglia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of action of antiviral agents, particularly those that are used in the treatment of viral infections of the eye.
the development of a mouse model for the study of ocular herpetic infection and the therapeutic effect of antiviral agents on this infection.
the pathogenesis of recurrent herpes simplex virus (type 1) ocular disease in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study demonstrate that aciclovir therapy is effective in reducing the incidence and persistence of HSV latency in trigeminal ganglion of infected mice.
aciclovir and, to a lesser degree, vidarabine are effective in reducing the incidence and/or severity of recurrent herpes simplex virus infection.
the antiviral therapy of herpes simplex virus (herpesvirus hominis) is effective in reducing the incidence or severity of recurrent disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of systemic antivirals for the treatment of recurrent ocular herpetic disease is not only safe but may have a significant impact on the course of the infection.
antiviral therapy can reduce the risk of recurrent ocular HSV.
the use of aciclovir or vidarabine after an ocular herpes infection in man may reduce the incidence of recurrent disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that antiviral drugs can reduce the incidence of latent herpes simplex virus in the trigemina ganglion after ocular infection.
we were able to demonstrate that antiviral drugs can reduce latent virus in the ganglion, and that the longer the treatment, the better the effect.
we were able to show that acyclovir can be used to treat latent HSV in the ganglia, which is the reservoir for recurrent ocular disease.
